limitations.flint: An event-root-finding consumer built but crashed with SIGSEGV in the GNU 16 hosted sandbox. The admitted consumer uses adaptive integration and dense output, both checked against exp(-t).
limitations.minres: minres_ez_t wrapper compiled but crashed in the hosted sandbox. The admitted consumer calls minres_solver with module callbacks; it passed solution/residual and changed-main checks.
limitations.parff: The pinned consumer compiled but crashed in the hosted sandbox. Investigation notes retain source, dependency locks and diagnostics.
limitations.forcad: GNU 16.2.0 internal compiler error in gfc_resolve_forall; newer source, two older releases and a fallback-guard patch all failed.
limitations.fortran_vector: The unmodified unique routine fails duplicate removal because it aliases an array element while compacting that array. The selected recipe uses the saved scalar first; original GNU 16 diagnostics are retained.
limitations.shunting-yard-fortran: The original internal callback layout crashed in the restricted GNU 16 sandbox. A checksum-guarded module-scope callback edit passes the five valid-expression checks. Global registrations and missing syntax validation remain upstream limitations.
limitations.fwalk: Archive contains symbolic links into its libcwalk Git submodule. Archive extraction rejects links and the submodule implementation is not contained in the archive. Requires an explicit, pinned C-submodule source adapter before an ordinary offline consumer can build. No sandbox build was submitted; no library changes made.
limitations.fregex: The original PCRE 1 API needs -lpcre. The default Debian 13 (trixie) main amd64 package index contains neither libpcre3 nor libpcre3-dev. PCRE2 is a different API, not a drop-in link substitution. Deferred pending an upstream PCRE2 port or an explicitly maintained native-library recipe.
limitations.time-f: Compiles, but the supplied strftime maximum length is ignored. The bounded-buffer probe expects zero for a 19-character date with maxsize=5, and fails. The C binding omits VALUE on size_t maxsize. The tm layout also needs platform ABI review before exposing mktime and timezone-dependent formatting; the source declares only nine integers. Deferred rather than publishing a limited example that hides these issues. A direct sandbox ABI probe confirms sizeof(struct tm)=56 bytes versus c_sizeof(time_f tm)=36 bytes.
limitations.flibcsv: The bounded CSV parser example compiles and passes quoted fields, embedded commas, an empty field and doubled quotes. Deferred before publication: the manifest license is the placeholder "license", no repository license file was found, and the Fortran wrapper has no explicit license notice; only bundled C sources identify LGPL-2.1-or-later. Source review also finds incorrect unused C bindings: entry_buf is a character rather than a C pointer, csv_strerror returns a character rather than a C pointer, and csv_write/csv_write2 omit VALUE on pointer arguments. Author clarification and a binding review are needed before presenting this as a ready-to-use library.

    real(kind = RPRE), dimension(:), intent(in) :: x
    real(kind = RPRE), intent(in), optional :: p

    if ((.not. present(p)) .or. (p .eq. 2.)) then
      norm1 = sqrt(sum(abs(x)**2))
    elseif (p .eq. 1.) then
      norm1 = sum(abs(x))
    else
      norm1 = (sum(abs(x)**p))**(1.0d0/p)
    end if
    return
  end function norm1

attempts.reason: The bounded CSV parser example compiles and passes quoted fields, embedded commas, an empty field and doubled quotes. Deferred before publication: the manifest license is the placeholder "license", no repository license file was found, and the Fortran wrapper has no explicit license notice; only bundled C sources identify LGPL-2.1-or-later. Source review also finds incorrect unused C bindings: entry_buf is a character rather than a C pointer, csv_strerror returns a character rather than a C pointer, and csv_write/csv_write2 omit VALUE on pointer arguments. Author clarification and a binding review are needed before presenting this as a ready-to-use library.
